summary: Zhang proves the arithmetic fundamental lemma for strongly regular semisimple elements over Q_p for p ≥ n (Theorem 15.1), together with the Jacquet–Rallis fundamental lemma for q ≥ n (Theorem 13.9), by induction on n through a global comparison. Modularity of arithmetic generating series of derived CM cycles on unitary Shimura varieties is matched with a regularized relative trace formula for partial Gaussian test functions, using that the Weil representation commutes with smooth transfer (Appendix A). Complete (cc-442dc5): every numbered statement is an item, every missing item is routed exactly once, and twenty-eight findings are recorded. The partial-Gaussian descent of §12.4 (E16, E17), the Gaussian normalization (E12, E15, corrected by Mihatsch–Zhang) and the Proposition 3.9 bound in the final induction (E28) are proof issues with repairs; the main theorems stand. Not formalised.

items.name: Hermitian-to-quadratic convention
items.statement: For a characteristic-zero quadratic extension F/F0, an F/F0-Hermitian form is linear in its first argument. Its F0-quadratic form is q(u)=h(u,u); its associated bilinear form is TrF/F0 h and has diagonal 2q. Norm fibres are Vξ={u:q(u)=ξ}.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct scalar restriction, trace bilinear form and norm fibres; distinguish the pairings by type.
Export orthogonal decomposition and isometry transport.

items.name: Schwartz spaces and Fourier transform
items.statement: Use locally constant compactly supported functions at nonarchimedean places and algebraically rapidly decreasing smooth functions at infinity. On quadratic vector spaces use ψ(⟨x,y⟩) and the self-dual Haar measure; assemble adelic restricted tensors.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct partial Fourier transforms and seminorm estimates; compare the positive Fourier sign with Mathlib's convention.

items.name: SL2 automorphic and coefficient-valued forms
items.statement: Over totally real F0, use h=n(b)m(a^(1/2))κθ and Wξ^(k)(h)=a^(k/2)exp(2πiξ(b+ia))exp(ikθ). Define fixed-level parallel-weight holomorphic forms, their algebraic q-structure, finite tensor-valued forms, and Aexp whose lowering image is holomorphic of weight k−2.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct adelic/classical conversion φ↦φ♭, Fourier coefficient and coefficient extension.
Require smoothness for absolute Fourier reconstruction, not mere continuity.

items.name: Group, Lie and semi-Lie relative spaces
items.statement: For n≥2 embed GL(n−1) diagonally in GLn. Define Sn={γ:γ conjugate(γ)=1}, sn={y:y+conjugate(y)=0}, and Sn−1×V′n−1, V′r=F0^r⊕(F0^r)*, with action (h⁻¹γh,h⁻¹u1,u2h). For unitary groups use V#=V⊕Fu0 with h(u0,u0)=1.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct actions, homogeneous/group adapters and block embeddings; expose ambient and acting ranks separately.

items.name: Relative orbit matching
items.statement: Regular semisimple linear relative orbits correspond to the disjoint union of unitary relative regular semisimple orbits over Hermitian isometry classes. Matching is F-conjugacy after the block embeddings; for semi-Lie pairs it is equality of characteristic coefficients and moments h(g^i u,u)=u2γ^i u1.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Invariant quotient and reciprocal polynomial
items.statement: An parametrizes monic conjugate-self-reciprocal degree-n polynomials with nonzero constant term; B records characteristic coefficients and moments. Preserve det(T+g) versus det(T−g) conventions. Irreducible α implies nonzero unitary vectors are cyclic; CM compactness is an additional condition.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct quotient map, discriminant open, sign adapter and refined invariants.

items.name: Orbital integrals and transfer factors
items.statement: Fix ηF/F0 and an extension η̃ to F×. Raw linear orbital integrals integrate Φ(h⁻¹·x)|det h|^sη(det h). §2 special values and derivatives include the cyclic-column transfer factor; unitary integrals are untwisted. Integral GL and hyperspecial U subgroups have volume one.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Separate raw integral, transferred value and transferred derivative.
For rank r semi-Lie use ω=η̃(det(γ)^−floor(r/2)det(u1,γu1,…,γ^(r−1)u1)); prove conjugation and measure-change laws.

items.name: Smooth and partial transfer
items.statement: Linear and unitary test functions match when transferred orbital integrals agree on matching regular semisimple orbits; use two local Hermitian classes nonarchimedean and all signatures over R. Partial transfer fixes α and one Hermitian class and requires vanishing on other classes in that fibre.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct the matching relation on test-function quotient spaces and split-place elementary transfer.
Existence is a theorem, not data assumed in the definition.

items.name: Group Jacquet–Rallis FL
items.statement: For unramified quadratic F/F0 of odd residue characteristic and q≥n, 1Sn(OF0) transfers to (1K0#,0) on the n-dimensional unitary spaces, with GL(n−1)(OF0) and K0 volumes one.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Semi-Lie Jacquet–Rallis FL
items.statement: Under the same unramified odd hypotheses and q≥n, the unit function on (Sn−1×V′n−1)(OF0) transfers to (1K0×Λ0,0), for the self-dual lattice Λ0 in split dimension n−1.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Maximal-order FL
items.statement: For a regular semi-Lie pair in the split space, if g is full-group regular semisimple and OF[g] is maximal in the degree-r étale algebra F[g], the unit-function FL holds.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: FL rank equivalence
items.statement: For q≥n in the unramified odd setting, group FL for Sn is equivalent to semi-Lie FL for Sn−1×V′n−1.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: FL norm-unit reduction
items.statement: Under Proposition2.7's hypotheses, group FL for Sn−1 implies dimension-(n−1) semi-Lie FL for vectors of unit norm.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Unitary Rapoport–Zink moduli
items.statement: For unramified F/F0 with odd residue characteristic, Nn classifies strict formal OF0-modules of relative height 2n and dimension n, OF-action of signature (n−1,1), relative principal polarization with conjugate Rosati, and height-zero polarized quasi-isogeny to a fixed supersingular framing object.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct base change, framing action and the relative/absolute height adapter; retain the relative polarization.

items.name: RZ representability and dimension
items.statement: Nn in the preceding unramified odd setting is formally locally of finite type and formally smooth of relative dimension n−1 over Spf O_Fbreve.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Framings, special Hom and diagonal
items.statement: Choose the signature-(1,0) object E, its conjugate action and canonical lifts as in §3.1. The framing decomposition gives δ:Nn−1→Nn with graph Δ⊂Nn−1×Nn. The polarized special rational Hom space Vn is nonsplit of dimension n with the last-factor unit vector.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Make conjugate action explicit rather than dropping overbars; construct adjoint, unit vector, orthogonal complement and δ.

items.name: Local KR divisor
items.statement: For nonzero u∈Vn, Z(u)⊂Nn is the locus where the special quasi-homomorphism lifts to an actual homomorphism. It is empty or a relative Cartier divisor, with gZ(u)=Z(gu) and Z(u0)≅Nn−1 for the unit vector.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct liftability under nilpotent base change, Cartier ideal and equivariance.

items.name: Derived group intersection
items.statement: For relative regular semisimple g∈U(Vn), Int(g)=χ(OΔ⊗L O(1×g)Δ) on Nn−1×Nn, using proper scheme intersection support and O_Fbreve-length.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct graph translate, derived support and finite-length Euler characteristic; prove conjugation invariance.

items.name: Derived fixed locus and semi-Lie intersection
items.statement: Ng=Γg∩ΔN is the naive fixed locus; LNg is the K-class OΓg⊗L OΔN transported to N. For regular semisimple (g,u), define Int(g,u)=χ(LNg⊗L OZ(u)); its support is a proper scheme.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Separate naive support from derived class; expose the projection formula on N×N.

items.name: Strong regular semisimplicity
items.statement: A semi-Lie regular semisimple pair is strongly regular if its group coordinate is semisimple under full-group conjugation. For relative group orbits require relative regularity and full GLn/U(Vn) semisimplicity. Do not identify these with mere relative regularity.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct the dense loci, cyclic-vector criteria and matching compatibility.

items.name: Strongly regular group AFL
items.statement: For F0=Qp, unramified quadratic F/F0, p odd and p≥n, matching γ∈Sn(F0)srs and g∈U(Vn)(F0)srs satisfy ∂Orb(γ,1Sn(OF0))=−Int(g)log p in the §2 normalization.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Strongly regular semi-Lie AFL
items.statement: Under Theorem15.1's literal indexed hypotheses p odd, F0=Qp and p≥n, matching strongly regular pairs in Sn−1×V′n−1 and U(Vn−1)×Vn−1 satisfy ∂Orb((γ,u′),1integral)=−Int(g,u)log p.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Maximal-order AFL input
items.statement: In the unramified odd local setting, for p>n and (g,u)∈(U(Vn−1)×Vn−1)srs with OF[g] maximal in F[g], semi-Lie AFL holds.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. (cc-442dc5) Finding E28: in the proof of Theorem 15.1 this is applied in Hermitian dimension n at places with p_v ≥ n only; the places with p_v ≤ n + 1 can be moved to case (ii) of Theorem 14.6.

items.name: Cayley and relative Schur maps
items.statement: On the invertibility opens, c(x)=−(1−x)(1+x)⁻¹ and c⁻¹(g)=(1+g)(1−g)⁻¹. For g′=[h u;w* d], set g=h+(1−d)⁻¹uw* and r(g′)=(g,u/((1−d)√ε)), with F=F0(√ε), ε∈OF0×; r♭ instead uses the Cayley vector ũ/√ε.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Make denominator domains explicit; construct central-scalar variants rξ and inverse chart.

items.name: Block Cayley identities
items.statement: In Lemma4.1's domain, ũ=2(1−d)⁻¹(1−g)⁻¹u, det(1−g′)=(1−d)det(1−g), and gw=((1−conjugate(d))/(1−d))u, with g the Schur complement above.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Relative Cayley open isomorphism
items.statement: Adding the lower-right Lie coordinate e gives an equivariant isomorphism U(Vn)°→(U(Vn−1)×Vn−1×u1)°; the same holds for r♭.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Cayley regularity and generic strong regularity
items.statement: On a unitary or linear chart, relative regularity of the source is equivalent to that of its image. Starting with strongly regular data, the images or inverse lifts are strongly regular for all but finitely many central scalars ξ or lower-right coordinates e.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: RZ graph pullback
items.statement: If 1−d is an OF-unit, (δ×δ)*Γg′=Γg∩π2*Z(u). For u≠0 the corresponding derived pullbacks have no higher Tor and factor through the graph and divisor classes.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Derived rank reduction
items.statement: Under the unit-denominator hypothesis with r(g′)=(g,u), u≠0, the derived class Δ∩L(id×g′)Δ equals LNg∩LZ(u). For relative regular semisimple g′, Int(g′)=Int(g,u).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Linear Cayley chart
items.statement: For γ′=[a b;c d]∈Sn put γ=a+(1−d)⁻¹bc. Use the Lie blocks y,b̃,c̃,e to define r and r♭ by (4.18)–(4.19), retaining the (1−y²)⁻¹ row correction, √ε factors and c̃ sign. Adjoining e gives the GL(n−1)-equivariant open isomorphism.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct inverse and invariant transport; visually recheck all barred formulas before Lean transcription.

items.name: Cayley matching
items.statement: Matching strongly regular inputs have matching rξ and r♭ξ images wherever defined as relative regular orbits. To retain strong regularity of the targets, impose the generic-ξ condition of Lemmas4.3 and4.9.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Orbital rank reduction
items.statement: For a norm-one ξ with 1−ξd and det(1−ξγ′) units, the raw group unit orbital integral equals the semi-Lie unit integral for every s. Transferred values/derivatives require the separate factor comparison.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: AFL rank equivalence
items.statement: For q≥n in the unramified odd setting, strongly regular group AFL for Sn is equivalent to semi-Lie AFL in dimension n−1.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: AFL norm-unit reduction
items.statement: Under Proposition4.12's hypotheses, group AFL for Sn−1 implies semi-Lie AFL in dimension n−1 for vectors of unit norm.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Vertex lattices and Deligne–Lusztig strata
items.statement: For the nonsplit unramified Hermitian space, vertex lattices satisfy Λ⊂Λ∨⊂ϖ⁻¹Λ with odd type t=dim(Λ∨/Λ). The closed stratum VΛ in Nred is smooth projective of dimension (t−1)/2; the reduced space is stratified by these loci.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct containment incidence, strata and group transport; export finite orbit types.

items.name: Stratum-cycle intersection is locally constant
items.statement: For n≥3, a maximal vertex lattice Λ and C∈CH1,VΛ(Nred), the function u↦χ(C⊗LZ(u)) on nonzero Vn is locally constant, compactly supported, and constant on a punctured neighbourhood of zero.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Fixed-g local constancy
items.statement: For full-group regular semisimple g, Int(g,u) is locally constant on vectors making (g,u) regular semisimple.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Characteristic-polynomial submersion
items.statement: At a strongly regular lift, the characteristic map in the relative Cayley coordinates (g,u,e) is a submersion as in Lemma5.4.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Joint local constancy of Int
items.statement: The function (g,u)↦Int(g,u) is locally constant on (U(Vn)×Vn)srs.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Compact support modulo conjugation
items.statement: The support of Int on the strongly regular semi-Lie locus is compact modulo U(Vn).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Unitary Shimura datum with CM torus
items.statement: For CM F/F0 and dimension n, take a CM type Φ and strict fake Drinfeld signature rφ0=n−1, rφ=n elsewhere in Φ. Construct GQ of rational similitudes and G̃=ZQ×GmGQ≅ZQ×ResF0/Q U(V), with reflex field E=EΦEr containing F.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct h(z), reflex field and product-level comparison; retain the positive CM-torus convention.

items.name: Integral level and bad-prime data
items.statement: D0 includes residual characteristic2, primes ramified in F/F0 and inert nonsplit V; D is a rational-prime pullback containing D0 and d its rational product. Away d choose self-dual Λv and hyperspecial KG,v; choose KZ maximal away d and small level at d.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct localization, adelic level factors and self-dual choices; prove independence under allowed conjugacy.

items.name: Auxiliary CM moduli
items.statement: The principally polarized OF-CM moduli M0 of type Φ is finite étale over OEΦ, under the paper's nonemptiness convention; the global discussion assumes some finite prime ramifies in F/F0 and selects a component. Add the specified level only at d.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Define the CM groupoid, component selection and level; compare its generic fibre with the torus canonical model.

items.name: RSZ integral unitary moduli
items.statement: Over OE[1/d], classify (A0,ι0,λ0,η0,A,ι,λ,η) with A0 in the selected CM moduli, OF[1/d]-action, strict fake Drinfeld determinant condition, prime-to-d principal polarization and KG,d-orbit of polarized rational Tate-Hom isometries. Impose the Eisenstein condition at the required places of F0 ramified over Q.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Define objects and d-isogeny morphisms, π1-invariant level sheaves and base change; compare all-primes generic Tate level.

items.name: RSZ smooth integral model
items.statement: The moduli in Definition6.1 is separated, finite type and smooth DM of relative dimension n−1 over OE[1/d]; sufficiently small level at d gives a smooth quasi-projective scheme, assumed thereafter.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Generic global KR divisors
items.statement: For ξ∈F0,+ and KG-orbit µ in V(A0,f), Z(ξ,µ) classifies the generic moduli point with u∈HomF°(A0,A), h(u,u)=ξ and η(u)∈µ. Weighted Z(ξ,φ) is the finite compact-support sum of proper pushforward divisor classes.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Correct morphisms to u′∘a0=ϕ∘u for the CM-source isomorphism a0 and ϕ:A→A′; define pushforward with multiplicities.

items.name: Integral global KR divisors
items.statement: Over OE[1/d] require u∈HomOF(A0,A)⊗Z[1/d], fixed positive norm and KG,d-level orbit. For φ=1Λ^d⊗φd define the weighted integral divisor; its generic fibre is the corresponding generic weighted divisor.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct integral liftability, corrected morphisms, finite orbit sums and generic-fibre compatibility.

items.name: KR forgetful map
items.statement: The KR forgetful morphism is representable, finite and unramified.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Flat Cartier KR divisors
items.statement: Étale locally on the ambient RSZ model, the KR morphism defines a Cartier divisor, flat over OE[1/d].
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Basic-locus p-adic uniformization
items.statement: At ν∤d over inert v0, the completed RSZ model is the quotient of the relative unitary RZ space times the away-v0 level cosets by the nearby global unitary group, with the CM-torus component factor as in (7.3)–(7.6).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Formal KR orbit expansion
items.statement: For positive ξ the pullback of Z(ξ,φ) to each CM-torus component of the basic completion is the finite sum over G′(F0)-orbits of (u,g) of φ^v0(g⁻¹u)[Z(u)×1gK^v0].
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Nonmaximal CM order
items.statement: Let α be irreducible, conjugate reciprocal and integral away d. Put F′=F[T]/α, extend conjugation by T↦T⁻¹, and explicitly assume F′ is CM over its totally real fixed field F0′. Set Rα=OF[1/d][T]/α and Ram(α) its nonmaximal-order places outside d.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct involution and local order, maximality test and finite bad set; the CM assumption is independent.

items.name: Naive and twisted fat CM moduli
items.statement: CM(α,g) parametrizes integral RSZ objects with ϕ∈EndOF(A)⊗Z[1/d], α(ϕ)=0, ϕ*λ=λ, and level intertwining by g∈G(F0,d). CM(α) is g=1. The order may be nonmaximal and no extra CM signature is imposed.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct forgetful map and double-coset dependence; retain potentially higher-dimensional special fibres.

items.name: Fat CM finite forgetful morphism
items.statement: For irreducible α as above, CM(α,g)→M is representable, finite and unramified.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Fat CM properness and good-order étaleness
items.statement: CM(α,g) is proper over OE[1/d], and finite étale away from Ram(α).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Rational characteristic polynomial
items.statement: For an abelian variety A over any field and rational endomorphism ϕ, det(T−ϕ|Vℓ A) lies in Q[T], has degree2dim A and is independent of ℓ≠char(k).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: F-linear characteristic polynomial
items.statement: With F-action and F-linear rational ϕ, its rank-n characteristic polynomial on Vℓ A lies in F[T] and is independent of ℓ.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Characteristic polynomial in connected families
items.statement: For an abelian scheme over a connected locally noetherian base, the rational characteristic polynomial of a quasi-endomorphism is constant; the F-linear polynomial is likewise constant when the F-action is present.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Hecke correspondence and fixed locus
items.statement: For g∈G(F0,d), Hk[KgK] classifies two RSZ objects with common CM factor and a polarized d-quasi-isogeny intertwining level by g. Its map to M×M is finite, each projection finite étale. Its fixed locus is the fibre product with the diagonal.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct both projections, finite correspondence and diagonal fixed functor; expose source/target quasi-isogeny direction.

items.name: Characteristic decomposition of fixed Hecke loci
items.statement: The Hecke fixed locus has a finite open-and-closed decomposition by F-characteristic polynomial. Each occurring polynomial is conjugate reciprocal and integral away d; for irreducible α its fibre is CM(α,g).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Derived CM cycle
items.statement: LCM(α,g) is [OHk⊗L OΔ] restricted to the open-and-closed CM(α,g) support, a rational supported G0-class. Weighted LCM(α,φ0) is the finite double-coset sum for φ0=1K^d⊗φ0,d.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Define restriction in support K-theory, weighted sum, and finite pushforward; do not replace the derived class by OCM.

items.name: Virtual dimension of derived CM
items.statement: LCM(α,g) lies in the dimension≤1 filtration F1G0(CM(α,g)) because the diagonal is regular of codimension n−1 and the correspondence is finite étale over M.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Formal Hecke uniformization
items.statement: On each basic CM-torus component, the completed Hecke correspondence is the nearby-group quotient of the RZ diagonal times the discrete away-v0 Hecke pair correspondence.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Naive CM uniformization
items.statement: The basic completion of CM(α) is the disjoint union of descended Nδ×1hK terms, indexed by nearby-group orbits (δ,h) with charδ=α and h⁻¹δh∈K away v0.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Derived CM uniformization
items.statement: The completed weighted derived CM class is the orbit sum φ0^v0(h⁻¹δh)[LNδ×1hK] on each CM-torus component.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Chow-valued special-divisor generating series
items.statement: Set Z(0,φ)=−φ(0)c1(ω). The adelic generating series sums Z(ξ,ω(hf)φ)Wξ^(n)(h∞) over totally positive ξ and the zero term, in CH1 of the generic unitary Shimura variety.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct the zero coefficient, Weil action and coefficient-valued q-expansion.

items.name: Chow modularity
items.statement: The preceding Chow-valued series is a holomorphic SL2 automorphic form of parallel weight n and level fixing φ, with the stated algebraic coefficient structure, over totally real F0.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Complex KR uniformization
items.statement: At a complex embedding ν of E, use the nearby Hermitian space indefinite only at its real restriction and the negative-line domain D. Each CM-torus component is G′(F0)\(D×G(Af)/K); positive-norm u gives D_u of negative lines perpendicular to u.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct the component and divisor quotients; compare with formal uniformization.

items.name: Complex KR orbit expansion
items.statement: For positive ξ, the complex divisor is the weighted descended sum φ(g⁻¹u)[D_u×1gK] over rational unitary orbits; it can be regrouped by stabilizer double cosets.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Kudla Green function
items.statement: For a negative line z, R(u,z)=h(u_z,u_z)=|h(u,z̃)|²/h(z̃,z̃)≤0. Put Ei(−r)=−∫r∞e^(−t)dt/t for r>0 and GK(u,h∞)(z)=−Ei(2πa_v R(u,z)) for u≠0 off D_u; set GK(0,h∞)=−log a_v.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct orthogonal projection, logarithmic singularity and descended orbit sum; preserve the parameter a_v.

items.name: Automorphic Green function and correction
items.statement: Use the automorphic Green function GB from Bruinier/Oda–Tsuzuki/BHKRY with its source-prescribed zero/nonpositive extensions; form the coefficient-wise correction GK−GB with the Whittaker factor as in (8.14).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Import an actual normalized Green function, not an arbitrary function satisfying modularity.
Close the source's omitted nonpositive-coefficient conventions before implementation.

items.name: Green-comparison modularity
items.statement: For F0=Q, the correction series evaluated at any complex Shimura point belongs to Aexp of weight n and Weil-stabilizer level.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Localized arithmetic divisor group
items.statement: For a regular flat arithmetic model over OE with finitely many places S removed, use Q-divisors plus compatible Green functions modulo (div f,−log|f|²). Removing S is quotienting by the classes supported above S.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct principal relations, vertical localization and pullback to proper arithmetic curves; use the same arithmetic-degree normalization as other height roadmaps.

items.name: Arithmetic KR series
items.statement: Equip positive KR divisors with GB; define the zero coefficient as −φ(0)c1(ω̂), with Petersson-metrized automorphic line bundle. Form the q-series in localized arithmetic CH1.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct arithmetic classes and level-dependent q-expansions; import generic metrized degree rather than duplicate it.

items.name: Arithmetic KR modularity over Q
items.statement: For F0=Q, the arithmetic series is holomorphic of weight n on Γ(N), with prime factors of N among the inverted primes, in the stated rational/algebraic coefficient space.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Proper-cycle arithmetic pairing
items.statement: Pair arithmetic CH1 with proper one-cycles on a regular flat arithmetic model, quotienting only vertical cycles rationally equivalent to zero on proper special-fibre subschemes. Over OE\S the value lies in R_S=R/spanQ{log p:S has a place above p}.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct proper-curve degree and vertical rational-equivalence descent; retain archimedean and residue-degree factors.

items.name: Derived CM class as a proper one-cycle
items.statement: Push F1G0(CM) to supported G0(M), pass to gr1, identify it rationally with CH1 supported on the CM image, and map to the proper-cycle quotient. Properness and zero-dimensional generic fibre are required.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct the filtration-preserving finite pushforward and cycle-class map; share the K-to-Chow comparison with SchemeKTheoryOperations.

items.name: Normalized arithmetic intersection series
items.statement: For Φ=φ0⊗φ, standard away d, set Int(τ,Φ)=(ẐB(τ,φ),LCM(α,φ0))/(τ(ZQ)[E:F]), where τ(ZQ)=#ZQ(Q)\ZQ(Af)/KZ. Its zero coefficient is the negative metrized Hodge pairing times φ(0).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct the component normalization, coefficientwise pairing and R_S-valued series.

items.name: Intersection-series modularity
items.statement: For F0=Q, Int(τ,Φ) is holomorphic of weight n and the specified level, with coefficients in R_S⊗Q Qbar.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: No generic intersection
items.statement: For irreducible α and nonzero ξ, the KR divisor and fat CM cycle do not intersect the generic fibre.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: No good split intersection
items.statement: Outside the bad set S with standard local test functions, a place split in F/F0 contributes no special-fibre intersection.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Good inert support is basic
items.statement: Outside S, at an inert place the intersection support is contained in the basic locus.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Local arithmetic intersection decomposition
items.statement: For nonzero ξ, the disjoint-generic-fibre pairing decomposes into local derived Euler lengths times log qν and Green evaluations at complex places with log qν=2, then sums over ν|v and divides by τ(ZQ)[E:F].
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct local terms and finite support; isolate zero coefficient from the positive series.

items.name: Inert local orbit formula
items.statement: At inert v0∤d with Φv0=1K×Λ, Int_v0(ξ,Φ)=2log q_v0 Σ[(δ,u)] Int_v0(δ,u)Orb((δ,u),Φ^v0), over nearby-group rational orbits of characteristic α and norm ξ.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Archimedean fixed point and orbit formula
items.statement: For δ of irreducible CM characteristic α in the nearby group, there is a unique fixed negative line zδ, and no nonzero rational u is perpendicular to it. The normalized archimedean Kudla intersection is the rational-orbit sum GK(u,h∞)(zδ)Orb((δ,u),Φ).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Refined CM Hermitian invariant
items.statement: The δ-action identifies V with restriction of scalars of a one-dimensional F′/F0′-Hermitian space W whose trace form is V. Define ξ′=q′(u)∈F0′ with TrF0′/F0 ξ′=ξ. The unique negative real embedding v′ gives R(u,zδ)=−|ξ′|v′.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct the trace-form equivalence and refined orbit invariant; relate conjugacy to ker(H1(T)→H1(G)).

items.name: Archimedean exponential-integral formula
items.statement: With the h∞-parameter retained, the archimedean local intersection is −Σ Ei(−2πa_v|ξ′|v′)Orb((δ,u),Φ). Equation(10.8) is its a_v=1 specialization.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Paired Green correction is modular
items.statement: For F0=Q, IntK−B(h,Φ), obtained by pairing the Green correction with the generic CM cycle and dividing by τ(ZQ)[E:F], is in Aexp of weight n and fixed Weil level; no integral model is needed for this correction.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Even-dimensional Weil representation
items.statement: For a nondegenerate even-dimensional quadratic space over the global base field, construct O(V)(A)×SL2(A) on Schwartz functions. Locally m(a) acts by χV(a)|a|^(d/2)φ(ax), n(b) by ψ(bq(x))φ(x), and w by γV times self-dual positive-sign Fourier transform, χV(a)=(a,(−1)^(d/2)det V).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Prove generator relations, orthogonal-sum and character changes, and splitting to SL2 in even dimension.

items.name: Theta convergence and rational invariance
items.statement: The theta sum Σu∈V(F)ω(g,h)φ(u) converges absolutely and is invariant under O(V)(F)×SL2(F).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Partially linearized automorphic kernel
items.statement: For affine X with reductive G-action and quadratic G-module V, fix a semisimple quotient fibre X(α). Define KΦ,α(g,h)=Σ(x,u)∈(X(α)×V)(F)ω(h)Φ(g⁻¹·(x,u)); its G(F)-quotient integral is SL2(F)-invariant when absolutely convergent.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct partial Weil action commuting with G and the kernel; attach convergence predicates before integration.

items.name: Unitary regular and singular orbit terms
items.statement: For irreducible α, split J into u≠0 regular terms and u=0 terms. A singular term carries vol(Gδ(F0)\Gδ(A0)) and integrates on Gδ(A0)\G(A0); Gδ is the anisotropic CM centralizer torus.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct stabilizer measures, unfolding and finite singular support.

items.name: Unitary orbital-sum convergence
items.statement: For any global Schwartz Φ the sum over relative regular rational orbits of ∫G(A)|Φ(g⁻¹·(δ,u))|dg is finite. For K∞-finite Φ, the fixed-α J is smooth and locally uniformly convergent in h.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Unitary Fourier orbit expansion
items.statement: The fixed-α unitary J unfolds as the sum of regular and centralizer-weighted singular terms. For ξ≠0 its ξ-Fourier coefficient is the orbit sum with q(u)=ξ.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Linear nilpotent orbit decomposition
items.statement: For irreducible α, the nonregular part of Sn(α)×V′ has three orbits: (0,0), nonzero column with zero row, and zero column with nonzero row. The last two have trivial stabilizers. Discard the zero orbit using nontrivial η on its stabilizer; regularize the other two.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct split quadratic form q(u1,u2)=u2u1, orbit classification and J_s's separated terms.

items.name: Linear regular-orbit convergence
items.statement: The regular rational-orbit sum of absolute linear orbital integrals converges locally uniformly for complex s; with K∞-finite Φ′ it is locally uniform in (h,s), and derivatives in s are justified.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Corrected Gaussian and partial Gaussian transfer
items.statement: Use the corrected positive Hermitian Gaussian exp(−2πq(u)) and rank-one linear φ′(x,y)=½(x+y)exp(−π(x²+y²)), with ψ(b)=exp(2πib). A partial Gaussian matches the positive-definite Gaussian for γ in a fixed compact subset Ω⊂Tnrs and vanishes on other signatures in that fibre.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Keep full Gaussian transfer, whose existence is only expected here, separate from the partial construction.
Implement the published scaling correction before checking weight or q-expansion.

items.name: Bessel and exponential-integral kernels
items.statement: For c>0 and complex s, Ks(c)=½∫0∞exp(−c(t+t⁻¹)/2)t^s dt/t. Use K−s=Ks, K1/2(c)=sqrt(π/(2c))e^−c and the source's order derivative; distinguish it from differentiation in c.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct holomorphic dependence on the order, differentiation bounds and Ei comparison.

items.name: Corrected rank-one orbital integral
items.statement: For ξ≠0, raw Orb((1,ξ),φ′,s)=|ξ|^((1−s)/2)[K(1−s)/2(2π|ξ|)+sgn(ξ)K(−1−s)/2(2π|ξ|)] with corrected φ′. At s=0 it is e^−2πξ for ξ>0 and zero for ξ<0; for ξ<0 its derivative is ½e^−2πξ Ei(−4π|ξ|).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Corrected rank-one Weil action
items.statement: For h=n(b)m(√a)κθ and ξ≠0, the transferred s=0 value is χ1(κθ)a^(1/2)e^(2πiξ(b+ia)) for ξ>0, and zero for ξ<0. For ξ<0 the derivative is half the same Whittaker factor times Ei(−4πa|ξ|).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Partial Gaussian descent chart
items.statement: Use GLn(R)=ANK with A=(R×)^n, N upper unipotent and K=SO(n). The proposed construction combines compact N/T cutoffs and a product of rank-one Gaussians. The map NK×Tnrs→Snc,rs has Weyl as well as sign identifications; the printed K∩A-torsor assertion is insufficient.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Replace the descent by genuine local slices or a proved Weyl-compatible pushforward, with correct multiplicities, sign character and Haar Jacobian.
Prove the constructed function is Schwartz and has the required orbital integral; this is an explicit open gate.

items.name: Partial Gaussian orbital factorization, conditional on repaired construction
items.statement: For γ∈Ω and a correctly descended normalized partial Gaussian, the orbital integral factors as the A-orbital integral of the product rank-one function; regular nilpotent terms obey the corresponding regularized formula.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Rank-one regularized global distribution
items.statement: For the split plane over F0 and nontrivial quadratic Hecke character η, J(φ′,s) is the regular orbit sum plus two nilpotent Tate terms. The 0+ term is L(s,η) times normalized local zeta integrals; the 0− term uses L(−s,η) and its corresponding signed parameter. The zero orbit contributes zero.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct analytic continuation of the two nilpotent terms and retain the ±s convention.

items.name: Normalized Tate factors
items.statement: For local Schwartz data, the Tate zeta integral divided by its L-factor extends to an entire function; at finite places it is a Laurent polynomial in q^s, and standard unramified data gives1. For nontrivial global η the completed global L-function is entire.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Rank-one regularized modularity
items.statement: J(ω(h)φ′,s) is smooth in h, entire in s, and left SL2(F0)-invariant.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Corrected Gaussian nilpotent factor
items.statement: For φ′=½(x+y)e^−π(x²+y²), the normalized archimedean 0+ Tate factor is½, and after h=n(b)m(√a)κθ it is ½χ1(κθ)a^((1−s)/2).
items.locator: Lemma12.11 with the published Gaussian correction
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Rank-one reduction over the CM fixed field
items.statement: For irreducible compact α, Sn(α)(F0) is one GLn-orbit with centralizer ResF0′/F0 Gm. The vector and covector become rank-one F0′ modules, with q=TrF0′/F0 q′; η∘det restricts to ηF′/F0′.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct the centralizer, trace pairing and character norm compatibility; compactness is equivalent to the CM condition.

items.name: Higher-rank nilpotent continuation
items.statement: The regular nilpotent local integrals divided by L(s,η′v) extend entirely, are Laurent polynomials at finite places, and equal1 at almost all places for fixed α and standard test data.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Higher-rank modularity of J_s
items.statement: For the fixed irreducible compact α, finite test data and correctly constructed partial Gaussian archimedean data, J(h,Φ′,s) is entire in s and left SL2(F0)-invariant.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Special-value and derivative expansion
items.statement: At s=0 define J and ∂J. The derivative is the sum of single-place derivative terms plus the derivative of the global nilpotent L-factors. For general rank use η′=ηF′/F0′ and retain the opposite sign when differentiating L(−s,η′).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct coefficientwise derivative and local decomposition with finite/nonzero support estimates; distinguish raw and transferred local terms.

items.name: Holomorphic coherent analytic series
items.statement: For totally positive-definite V, unitary Gaussian data and matching partial linear Gaussians, J(h,Φ) and J(h,Φ′) lie in holomorphic parallel-weight-n fixed-level spaces.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Coherent comparison from lower-rank FL
items.statement: With the finite set S and test functions of §13.2, assume group FL for Sn at every place outside S. Then E=J(Φ′)−J(Φ)=0 and all its nonzero Fourier orbit sums agree.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Unit-index Fourier vanishing criterion
items.statement: For a continuous SL2(F0)-invariant function right-invariant under K whose components at finite B are the conductor-conjugate hyperspecial groups of (13.3), vanishing of every nonzero ξ-Fourier coefficient with v(ξ)=0 for all v∈B forces the function to be constant; nonzero parallel weight forces zero.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Isolation of one rational invariant
items.statement: Fix b0∈B(F0), a split finite place v1 and compact neighbourhood constraints at all other places, standard integral at almost all. A sufficiently small neighbourhood at v1 leaves b0 as the only rational invariant in the adelic product.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Individual coherent orbital equality
items.statement: Under Theorem13.4's hypotheses, matching rational regular pairs of irreducible characteristic α and nonzero norm have equal global orbital integrals.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Local-to-global approximation for FL/AFL
items.statement: For strongly regular local data with integral characteristic polynomial, unit det(1−g) and nonzero norm, use Cayley, polynomial weak approximation and a totally real degree-n extension to construct a CM field, a rank-one Hermitian trace form and rational data arbitrarily close locally, preserving the integral étale order.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Prove field-algebra stability under close separable coefficients, positivity at infinity and simultaneous local Hermitian conditions.
Track a split versus nonsplit local target separately.

items.name: Final FL induction and density extension
items.statement: The group and semi-Lie FL conclusions hold for q≥n in the unramified odd setting; extension from strongly regular nonzero-norm data to all relative regular orbits uses orbital-integral local constancy.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Split derivative terms vanish
items.statement: In the incoherent test-function setup of §14, a split finite place v has ∂Jv(h,Φ′)=0.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Archimedean derivative detects one negative embedding
items.statement: For invertible refined ξ′, the corrected partial-Gaussian value is nonzero only when every local real component is positive; if ξ′ is not totally positive, its first derivative vanishes unless exactly one component is negative. In that case it is ½ times the corrected Whittaker factor times Ei(−4πa|ξ′|negative).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Archimedean arithmetic/analytic comparison obligation
items.statement: The intended identity is IntK_v(ξ,Φ)=−2 times the appropriately Whittaker-normalized archimedean derivative coefficient for matching data. The printed formulas mix parameters and Gaussian scales; the corrected comparison must include the change from Ei(−2πa|ξ′|) to Ei(−4πa|ξ′|) in the revised analytic convention.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Holomorphic corrected derivative
items.statement: For F0=Q and compatible corrected conventions, ∂Jhol=2∂J+IntK−B is holomorphic of weight n and common Weil level.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Conditional global arithmetic comparison
items.statement: With F0=Q and §14.3's S and standard good-place data, assume strongly regular group AFL for Sn over Qp at every p∉S. Then E♭=∂Jhol♭+Int vanishes in the fixed-level holomorphic space over R_S⊗Q Qbar.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. (cc-442dc5) Case (i) of the proof relies on item 23 beyond its printed bound; see E28 for the repair.

items.name: Individual local arithmetic comparison
items.statement: Under Theorem14.6's assumptions, for every finite v∉S and ξ≠0, −2∂Jv(ξ,Φ′)=Intv(ξ,Φ) as an equality in Q log pv.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Orbitwise AFL from the global comparison
items.statement: Under the same induction assumption, at inert v∉S and for matching rational strongly regular pairs with nonzero norm, −∂Orb((γ,u′),1integral)=Intv(δ,u)log qv.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Final AFL induction obligation
items.statement: Theorem15.1's group and semi-Lie endpoints21–22 follow by rank induction, CM globalization, the corrected global comparison and joint local constancy on the strongly regular locus. No extension to arbitrary p-adic base fields or all relative regular elements is inferred.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Weil action preserves smooth transfer
items.statement: For a local quadratic extension F/F0 and matching test functions on Sn×V′n and U(V)×V, ω(h) preserves matching for h∈SL2(F0); likewise on fixed-α partial transfers.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Hermitian Weil constants
items.statement: For an n-dimensional Hermitian space regarded as a 2n-dimensional quadratic space, χV(a)=η(a)^n and γV=η(detHerm V)ε(η,½,ψ)^n. The split vector/covector quadratic space has χ=γ=1.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Formal support of a coherent sheaf
items.statement: For a noetherian formal scheme X and closed formal Y defined by J, a coherent sheaf is formally supported on Y if annihilated by some J^m. Affinely, for I-complete A and Y defined by J, this is algebraic support of its finite A-module in Spec(A/J), not only the topological support in Spf A.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct supported coherent categories, change of ideal and finite-thickening equivalence.

items.name: Coherent and supported perfect Grothendieck groups
items.statement: Define G0(X) from coherent sheaves and K0^Y(X) from bounded complexes of finite locally free sheaves with homology formally supported on Y. Use the existing exact-category Grothendieck group as the algebraic presentation; the formal coherent/perfect categories still require construction.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct relations, class maps, exact functoriality, cup product and support change; distinguish globally strictly perfect from locally perfect unless a resolution property is proved.

items.name: Dimension and codimension filtrations
items.statement: For supported K0, Fi is generated by supports of codimension at least i; for coherent G0, Fi is generated by sheaves supported in dimension at most i. Form the associated gradeds, with rational coefficients throughout the paper.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct monotonicity, boundedness and finite-pushforward compatibility; interpret unions through directed finite unions of supports.

items.name: Regular supported K/G comparison
items.statement: For regular pure-dimensional finite-dimensional X in a category with the required resolution/devissage theorem, K0^Y(X)≅G0(Y) and F^(d−i) corresponds to Fi. The formal-scheme extension requires verification, not an automatic consequence of scheme devissage.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Scheme rational Adams decomposition
items.statement: For the regular schemes in Gillet–Soulé's hypotheses, supported rational K0 decomposes into Adams weight spaces, and the codimension filtration is the sum of weights at least its index.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Scheme support-filtration multiplication
items.statement: Under the scheme hypotheses of Gillet–Soulé[11] Proposition5.5, F^j1K0^Y(X)Q · F^j2K0^Z(X)Q ⊂ F^(j1+j2)K0^(Y∩Z)(X)Q.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Locally noetherian formal K-groups
items.statement: For an increasing directed cover by noetherian formal opens Xi, define the paper's K0, G0 and supported K0 as inverse limits along restrictions, together with their filtrations. Verify independence of the exhaustion and identify the comparison with a global categorical construction where available.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct restriction systems and canonical comparison maps; do not confuse this open-exhaustion limit with continuous K-theory of nilpotent thickenings.

items.name: Proper torsion Euler degree
items.statement: For W a scheme proper over Spf A, A a complete DVR, define degree([E])=Σi(−1)^i lengthA Riπ*E; the scheme-over-Spf and properness assumptions force finite-length cohomology. For derived intersections sum (−1)^(i+j)length Riπ*Torj.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct additive Euler degree, supported derived pairing and base-change length formula.

items.name: Closed-union G0 decomposition modulo overlap
items.statement: For a scheme-theoretic closed union X=X1∪X2 with I1∩I2=0, G0(X) modulo the image of G0(X1∩X2) identifies with the direct sum of the two component quotients. Quotients mean cokernels, not assumed injective embeddings.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Expected-dimensional Tor vanishing
items.statement: Let X be locally noetherian formal of pure finite dimension, Zi pure-dimensional closed subschemes, Z1→X regular and Z2 Cohen–Macaulay. If the intersection has expected codimension at every point, Tori^OX(OZ1,OZ2)=0 for i>0 and derived tensor equals ordinary tensor in G0.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Tor vanishing on an expected component
items.statement: Under LemmaB.2's ambient hypotheses, if Z1∩Z2=Y∪Y′ with Y of expected dimension, higher Tor restricted to Y vanishes in G0(Y) modulo the image from Y∩Y′.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Supported K-to-Chow comparison
items.statement: For the regular arithmetic schemes used in §9, the rational dimension-one associated graded of coherent K-theory with prescribed support identifies with the corresponding supported Chow group, compatibly with finite proper pushforward.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Chow operations for the cycle construction
items.statement: Use rational equivalence, proper pushforward with residue multiplicities, flat/lci pullback, Chern classes and projection/excess-intersection formulas on the actual schemes/stacks in the moduli problem; a finite unramified divisor map need not be a closed immersion.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Import the generic Chow operations once and verify each morphism's proper/flat/lci conditions.

items.name: Existing abstract exact Grothendieck group
items.statement: TauCeti.ExactK0 E is the free abelian group on object isomorphism classes in an essentially small additive category with exact structure E, modulo conflation relations. It is a reusable carrier, not formal-scheme G0 by itself.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Reuse the class map and conflation-additive universal property after constructing the appropriate exact category.

items.name: Existing regular-sequence carrier
items.statement: Mathlib's RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular M rs requires successive scalar multiplication to be regular on the preceding quotient and the final quotient to be nonzero. It supplies the algebraic predicate, not the Koszul resolution or formal Tor theorem.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Reuse IsWeaklyRegular and IsRegular; prove the source's commutative-algebra consequences separately.

items.name: Existing real Gaussian Fourier formula
items.statement: For complex b with positive real part, the real Fourier transform of exp(−πbx²) is b^(−1/2)exp(−πt²/b), in Mathlib's real Fourier convention.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Existing real-line Poisson formula
items.statement: For a complex-valued Schwartz function f on R, Σn∈Z f(x+n)=Σn∈Z Fourier(f)(n)e(nx). This is not the adelic Poisson theorem used in §12.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Existing dominated parameter differentiation
items.statement: Under neighbourhood-wise a.e. differentiability, measurability and an integrable bound on the derivatives, differentiation commutes with the integral at the specified parameter, and the derivative integrand is integrable.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Existing Schur determinant identity
items.statement: For square blocks over a commutative ring, with the bottom-right block D invertible, det([A B;C D])=det(D)det(A−BD⁻¹C).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Existing Cayley–Hamilton theorem
items.statement: A square matrix over a commutative ring annihilates its characteristic polynomial.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Conjecture 3.2 (statement only)
items.statement: (a) If γ ∈ S_n(F_0)_rs matches g ∈ U(V_n)(F_0)_rs, then ∂Orb(γ, 1_{S_n(O_{F_0})}) = −Int(g)·log q. (b) If (γ, u′) ∈ (S_n × V′_n)(F_0)_rs matches (g, u) ∈ (U(V_n) × V_n)(F_0)_rs, then ∂Orb((γ, u′), 1_{(S_n × V′_n)(O_{F_0})}) = −Int(g, u)·log q. The arithmetic fundamental lemma on all regular semisimple elements; the paper proves the strongly regular case (Conjecture 3.8, Theorem 15.1), and Remark 4.13 notes the analogue of Proposition 4.12.
